asks.held_by: USCIS
asks.title: H-1B cap-exempt status by employer
asks.collected_on: Form I-129, which records whether a petition is cap-exempt and on what ground.
asks.published_now: National totals by exemption category in the Report to Congress. The H-1B Employer Data Hub names every employer and carries no cap field.
asks.request: The Employer Data Hub extract with two added fields, cap-exempt yes or no and the exemption ground, by employer and fiscal year, with approvals and denials.
asks.would_settle: Which employers use the exemption, at what scale, and whether use is concentrated. Today the petitions filed under the affiliated-nonprofit ground cannot be attributed to any organization.

evidence.label: employers on a cap-exempt list built by inference, not by record

asks.held_by: NSF National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics
asks.title: Federal graduate support by citizenship
asks.collected_on: Survey of Graduate Students and Postdoctorates, which records support by mechanism and agency and enrolment by citizenship. Survey of Earned Doctorates, which records primary support by citizenship.
asks.published_now: Support by agency, and enrolment by citizenship, never together. The SED records the assistantship but not which award paid for it.
asks.request: A tabulation of graduate students with federal support, by citizenship status and by field, from existing returns. If the returns do not link the two, a statement saying so, which would itself settle whether the figure exists.
asks.would_settle: What federal research funding spends per doctoral student by citizenship. It would turn a proxy into a measurement.

asks.held_by: NSF National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics
asks.title: Citizens and permanent residents separated at conferral
asks.note: Master's degrees would need a change to IPEDS and are a separate ask, below.
asks.collected_on: Survey of Earned Doctorates, which records citizenship status at conferral in three categories.
asks.published_now: Two categories: citizens and permanent residents combined, and temporary visa holders. The Survey of Doctorate Recipients separates them after graduation but not at the degree.
asks.request: SED doctorate counts by field and year with US citizens and permanent residents shown separately.
asks.would_settle: The citizen share of US graduate STEM doctorates, which no published source reports.

asks.held_by: DHS Student and Exchange Visitor Program
asks.title: OPT and STEM OPT for every institution
asks.collected_on: SEVIS.
asks.published_now: A Top 100 ranking of schools. A school outside it is absent rather than zero, so school totals are a floor and year-to-year movement may only reflect the cutoff moving.
asks.request: OPT and STEM OPT authorisation counts for every certified school, by calendar year, on the same basis as the published national table.
asks.would_settle: Work-authorisation participation for every institution, not just the hundred largest.

asks.held_by: No federal agency. The natural home is the National Center for Education Statistics.
asks.title: Graduate applications and admissions
asks.collected_on: Nothing. The IPEDS Admissions component covers first-time undergraduates only.
asks.published_now: Degrees conferred. No federal collection records who applied to a graduate program, who was admitted, or who was offered funding.
asks.request: A graduate admissions component in IPEDS: applications, admissions and funded offers by broad field and residency status.
asks.would_settle: Whether domestic applicants are declining, being declined, or not applying. That is the question behind this whole project and the one it cannot answer.

asks.held_by: USCIS
asks.title: L-1 and O-1 petitions by employer
asks.collected_on: Form I-129, the same form and system that produce the published H-1B Employer Data Hub.
asks.published_now: Nothing by employer. Neither classification requires a labor condition application, so the Labor Department never sees them, and USCIS publishes employer hubs for H-1B, H-2A and H-2B only.
asks.request: Petitioner name and address for L-1A, L-1B, O-1A and O-1B, aggregated by petitioner and fiscal year, with approvals and denials. The H-1B hub's extract, run for four more classifications.
asks.would_settle: Which companies transfer the most staff into the United States without a wage test, and whether O-1 growth sits in the industries most constrained by the H-1B cap.

asks.held_by: DHS Student and Exchange Visitor Program; the State Department for visa issuance
asks.title: F-1 students by institution
asks.collected_on: SEVIS, which records every F-1 student against a certified school.
asks.published_now: State reports issuance by consulate and nationality, never by school. SEVP publishes school-level figures for OPT alone. IPEDS reports non-resident enrolment, a residency category rather than a visa count.
asks.request: Active F-1 student records by certified school and year, split by education level.
asks.would_settle: Where the student pipeline enters. That is the first stage of everything else on this page.

asks.held_by: State Department for visa issuance; DHS for admissions
asks.title: Country of birth for nonimmigrant classes
asks.collected_on: The nonimmigrant visa application, which records place of birth alongside nationality.
asks.published_now: Every visa and admission series is by nationality. A naturalised citizen of one country born in another cannot be distinguished from a native-born citizen anywhere in the published data.
asks.request: Nonimmigrant visa issuances by visa class, fiscal year, nationality and country of birth. For classes admitted without a visa, the equivalent from DHS admission records if they carry birthplace.
asks.would_settle: How far a nationality series reflects the country people actually come from. In the one dataset that publishes both fields, the two disagree often enough to matter, and the largest single citizenship among the mismatches is Canada.

evidence.label: filings where citizenship and birth country differ, where both are published

asks.held_by: Department of Labor, Office of Foreign Labor Certification
asks.title: Restore the worker fields to the PERM disclosure file
asks.note: This is the single most consequential item on the page. The collection did not change. Only the release did.
asks.collected_on: Form ETA-9089, on which the employer still answers all three questions.
asks.published_now: Nothing. Country of citizenship, country of birth and class of admission were all published through FY2024 and all three were removed at once in FY2025, when the file went from 155 columns to 137.
asks.request: The three withdrawn columns, restored to the quarterly disclosure file on the basis used through FY2024.
asks.would_settle: Every question about who fills a sponsored post. This site can say that a Washington state agency sponsored a Hong Kong citizen for permanent residence in FY2021. It cannot say whether that still happens, and no future harvest will tell us, because the field is gone rather than empty.

evidence.label: window, and it cannot be extended

asks.held_by: USCIS
asks.title: A stable employer identifier in the H-1B Employer Data Hub
asks.collected_on: Form I-129, which carries the petitioner's FEIN.
asks.published_now: The employer name as filed, and nothing else. There is no key that survives a spelling change.
asks.request: Any stable per-employer identifier alongside the name. A hashed or truncated FEIN would do. The agency need not publish the number itself, only something that is the same across filings by the same body.
asks.would_settle: Counting an employer at all. Cognizant files under eighteen spellings and the largest accounts for 22,287 of 50,994. Every employer total published anywhere, by anyone, is a floor, and the error is largest for exactly the biggest filers.

asks.held_by: USCIS
asks.title: Name the affiliated nonprofits in the Report to Congress
asks.collected_on: Form I-129.
asks.published_now: A count of petitions from nonprofits related to or affiliated with an institution of higher education. No organization is named.
asks.request: The same count, broken out by petitioning organization.
asks.would_settle: Sizing the bodies running the cap-exempt route. This site reaches for IRS Form 990 to do it, which gives revenue and headcount but says nothing about cap status, so the two can sit side by side and never join.

asks.held_by: Department of Labor, Office of Foreign Labor Certification
asks.title: A six-digit NAICS code on the labor condition application
asks.collected_on: Form ETA-9035, on which the employer reports NAICS.
asks.published_now: Whatever depth the employer chose. The same industry appears at two, four, five and six digits in a single file.
asks.request: Validation requiring six digits at filing, and the full six-digit code in the disclosure file.
asks.would_settle: Separating a staffing firm from a law firm, which is the whole basis of the body-shop test. A filing coded '6111' is a school and cannot be counted as one, because '6111' covers several six-digit industries and assigning it would be a guess.

evidence.label: distinct NAICS codes, at mixed depths

asks.held_by: Department of Labor, Office of Foreign Labor Certification
asks.title: A published column schema, and a diff when it changes
asks.note: Not a request for data. It would cost close to nothing and it is the cheapest item here.
asks.collected_on: Not applicable. This is about the release, not the form.
asks.published_now: Files whose column names change between years without notice. H_1B_DEPENDENT became H-1B_DEPENDENT in FY2025. FW_INFO_BIRTH_COUNTRY became FOREIGN_WORKER_BIRTH_COUNTRY in FY2020.
asks.request: A versioned schema published with each release, and a diff against the previous one.
asks.would_settle: A whole category of silent error. A renamed column read by its old name returns no value, and a missing dependency flag reads as a firm that is never dependent. That is a wrong answer rather than a crash, and no downstream check can catch it reliably.

asks.held_by: Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
asks.title: The complete H-1B enforcement case set
asks.collected_on: WHISARD case management.
asks.published_now: An extract carrying the largest cases only.
asks.request: All concluded H-1B cases with employer, fiscal year, violation type and back wages, at the division's usual thresholds.
asks.would_settle: Reading absence. A firm that does not appear may have had no findings or may have had small ones, and the extract cannot distinguish them. Only a handful of employers match between the enforcement file and the wage data, so the crossing is inconclusive.

asks.held_by: DHS SEVP holds the authorisations; Treasury holds the payroll
asks.title: A wage measure for OPT employment
asks.collected_on: SEVIS records the authorisation. No federal collection records what the job pays.
asks.published_now: Nothing.
asks.request: Aggregate earnings for OPT-authorised employment, by year and broad field. A tabulation from the employer side of the payroll tax would do it without a new survey.
asks.would_settle: Sizing the payroll-tax differential. OPT employment is exempt from the employer share of FICA, which is a real price difference against an equivalent citizen hire. This site publishes no national total for it, only a per-$100,000 figure and a scenario grid, because the wage base does not exist.

asks.held_by: DHS Office of Immigration Statistics
asks.title: Country of birth crossed against country of residence
asks.collected_on: Admission and adjustment records.
asks.published_now: Yearbook tables 2 and 3, which are separate totals for the same population.
asks.request: The cross-tabulation of the two, at the usual thresholds.
asks.would_settle: Whether a surplus in one country can be attributed to a particular origin. No individual is traced across the two tables, so however strongly the deficits in one line up with the surpluses in another, the inference cannot be made, and this site does not make it.

asks.held_by: NSF National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics
asks.title: State geography on the Survey of Doctorate Recipients
asks.collected_on: The SDR questionnaire, which records location.
asks.published_now: Nothing below national. State is suppressed in the public-use file for confidentiality.
asks.request: A state-level tabulation of the core SDR measures with the usual cell suppression. Not the microdata.
asks.would_settle: Every state-level question about the doctoral workforce. This site publishes a page for each of the fifty states and cannot put a single SDR figure on any of them.

asks.held_by: NSF National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics
asks.title: Hours worked, above the topcode
asks.collected_on: The SDR questionnaire.
asks.published_now: HRSWKP topcoded at more than 40, so 41 hours and 80 hours are a single value.
asks.request: Either a higher topcode or a banded distribution above forty.
asks.would_settle: The claim people actually make. The argument is about the distance above forty, and the variable collapses exactly the range the argument is about.

asks.held_by: National Center for Education Statistics
asks.title: Permanent residents separated from citizens in IPEDS enrolment
asks.note: This is a change to the collection, not only to the release, which is why it is marked as new. The doctorate version of the same question needs no new collection and is above.
asks.collected_on: The IPEDS Fall Enrolment component, which collects 'non-resident alien' as a residency category.
asks.published_now: Two groups, with permanent residents counted as domestic and reported under race and ethnicity.
asks.request: A permanent-resident category in Fall Enrolment and Completions.
asks.would_settle: Measuring the foreign-born share of a program. Every non-resident share on this site is a floor, and the gap is largest in exactly the fields where the question is asked most.

asks.held_by: National Center for Education Statistics
asks.title: Graduate borrowing in Student Financial Aid
asks.collected_on: The IPEDS Student Financial Aid component, which covers undergraduates.
asks.published_now: Undergraduate Pell and federal loans. Graduate borrowing sits in the Education Department's loan systems and not in IPEDS.
asks.request: Graduate federal loan volume by institution and year in Student Financial Aid, or a crosswalk to the loan data.
asks.would_settle: Putting a federal dollar figure beside a graduate program. A graduate-heavy institution's federal money is understated on this site, and the borrowing that funds a terminal master's is invisible.

asks.held_by: Bureau of Labor Statistics
asks.title: Raise or remove the OEWS wage topcode
asks.collected_on: The OEWS survey.
asks.published_now: Wages topcoded at $239,200 and published as '#', with suppressed cells as '*'.
asks.request: A higher topcode, or the mean above it, for occupations where the topcode binds.
asks.would_settle: Comparing a high-wage occupation against its prevailing wage. A topcoded occupation has no usable 90th percentile, so the comparison this site runs on every certified filing drops out for the occupations where the money is.

evidence.label: filings priced against the local median
of those, paid below the local median for the occupation

asks.held_by: Department of Justice, National Security Division
asks.title: Resume the research-security case compilation
asks.collected_on: Case records.
asks.published_now: Nothing after 19 November 2021. The compilation stopped there and the China Initiative ended on 23 February 2022.
asks.request: Resumed publication on the previous basis, or a statement that it has been discontinued.
asks.would_settle: Saying anything about the present. This site publishes the register as a frozen record and labels it as one, because the alternative is to let a 2021 snapshot read as a current picture. Cases have been brought since and none is in a public list.

evidence.label: of them brought after the list stopped

asks.held_by: Internal Revenue Service, Tax Exempt and Government Entities
asks.title: Restore the Form 990 e-file years that came off irs.gov
asks.note: The counts of what went missing come from outside researchers, not from the IRS, and the agency has published no reconciliation. A statement of what is held and what is not would itself be useful.
asks.collected_on: Form 990, filed electronically.
asks.published_now: Tax years 2019 onward on irs.gov. The 2009 to 2018 e-file XML sat on an AWS public bucket that stopped updating at the end of 2021, and outside researchers report that filings did not survive the move.
asks.request: The full e-file XML archive back to the start of electronic filing, hosted by the agency, with an index of what is held.
asks.would_settle: Any long-run analysis of a nonprofit. A sponsoring organization's growth over fifteen years is the question worth asking, and the public record of it now depends on third-party mirrors.

asks.held_by: Department of Education; the National Center for Education Statistics would be the natural keeper of the register
asks.title: A public deposit requirement for federally funded dissertations and theses
asks.note: This is the gap that shaped the whole project. Building the dissertation record meant visiting institutions one at a time, because there is no list. Several publish nothing searchable at all. Coverage here is therefore a floor and the absence is not evenly spread -- a university that posts less is not a university that awards less.
asks.collected_on: Nothing. No federal rule obliges a university to publish a dissertation or a thesis, or to list the ones it has awarded. Each institution decides, and the decision is revisited department by department.
asks.published_now: Whatever each university chooses to post. There is no federal register of awarded doctorates and no national index of where a dissertation can be read. ProQuest holds the largest collection and it is a private subscription product.
asks.request: A deposit rule with the grant money: a doctorate or a master's thesis completed with any federal support is lodged in a public repository within a year of the award, with the author, the institution, the department, the year and the advisor in a machine-readable record. No paywall. A single federal index of those records.
asks.would_settle: Who is actually being trained, where, in what, and on whose money. This is the foundation under every other ask on this page, and it is the one the public most obviously already paid for.

evidence.label: of them with no public repository the harvest could find
reachable only through a handle or DOI resolver, not a browsable index

asks.held_by: Department of Education, National Center for Education Statistics
asks.title: Graduate admissions by citizenship, residency and program
asks.collected_on: Nothing at this grain. IPEDS collects admissions for undergraduates and enrollment by a coarse nonresident-alien flag. It does not collect graduate admissions by citizenship at all.
asks.published_now: Graduate enrollment by the nonresident flag, at institution level, with no admissions figures beneath it.
asks.request: Per institution, per program, per year: applications, admissions and matriculations, split by US citizen and permanent resident, in-state, out-of-state, and temporary visa holder. Counts only, at the existing suppression thresholds.
asks.would_settle: Whether an American applicant and a foreign applicant to the same program face the same odds. Nothing published today can answer that, so the argument is conducted entirely on enrollment -- which is an outcome, and cannot separate who applied from who was chosen.

evidence.label: institutions where the project can show the enrollment outcome but not the admissions decision behind it

asks.held_by: Department of Labor, Office of Foreign Labor Certification
asks.title: The PERM worker fields, restored
asks.note: The Vice President described PERM on 2026-10-08 as the mechanism by which an H-1B holder stays permanently. That is the mechanism whose worker detail stopped being published the same year.
asks.collected_on: Form ETA-9089, which records the worker's citizenship, country of birth, the visa held at the time of filing, and the offered wage.
asks.published_now: Nothing. The FY2025 disclosure file dropped every worker field. The layout went from 155 columns to 137 and the citizenship column is among those removed.
asks.request: Restore the worker fields to the quarterly disclosure file. They were published without incident for twelve years.
asks.would_settle: Everything this project can say about who the public sector sponsors for permanent residence, it can say only up to FY2024. PERM is the only federal disclosure file that carries a worker's citizenship, and as of FY2025 that series has ended.

evidence.label: certified public-employer filings the series covers, FY2013 to FY2024

asks.held_by: Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division; Treasury holds the matching payroll record
asks.title: Wages actually paid on an H-1B, not the wage offered
asks.collected_on: The LCA records an offered wage and a prevailing wage. What the worker is actually paid appears on a W-2, which Treasury holds and Labor does not.
asks.published_now: Offered wages, in the disclosure files. No agency publishes what was paid.
asks.request: A tabulation, built from matched W-2 and LCA records, of median wage actually paid against the prevailing wage for the same occupation, area and year. By employer where the cell clears the threshold, otherwise by occupation and area. No person-level record.
asks.would_settle: Whether the wage gap argued about in public is real and how large it is. Every figure on this site is an offered wage, because that is the only wage published -- and an offer is a ceiling on intent, not evidence of a payment.

evidence.label: OPT and STEM OPT authorizations in the year the exemption applies to

asks.held_by: DHS Student and Exchange Visitor Program
asks.title: SEVIS by school, program, level and country of citizenship
asks.collected_on: SEVIS, continuously. Every F-1 and J-1 record carries the school, the program of study, the level and the country of citizenship, and is updated each term.
asks.published_now: Quarterly totals by school and by country, in separate tables that cannot be crossed. The published school table does not carry country; the country table does not carry school.
asks.request: One table, annually: school, program level, two-digit CIP, country of citizenship, active records. Counts only, at SEVP's own suppression threshold.
asks.would_settle: Which programs at which schools draw from which countries. Today the two halves are published separately and the join is exactly the part that would answer the question.

asks.held_by: DHS Student and Exchange Visitor Program
asks.title: OPT and STEM OPT authorizations by employer
asks.note: An H-1B petition names its employer and is published. The OPT authorization that usually precedes it names its employer on the form and is not.
asks.collected_on: Form I-983 for STEM OPT, which names the employer, and the SEVIS record, which carries the authorization and the school.
asks.published_now: National totals. No employer appears in any published OPT table.
asks.request: Employer, school, year and count of authorizations, for OPT and STEM OPT separately. Counts only.
asks.would_settle: Who employs the graduates of the programs this site measures, in the window before an H-1B is filed. OPT is the largest foreign-worker programme in the country by headcount and it is the one with no employer-level disclosure at all.

asks.held_by: Internal Revenue Service
asks.title: The payroll tax forgone on F-1 and J-1 employment
asks.collected_on: Employment tax filings. A student on F-1 or J-1 in practical training is exempt from Social Security and Medicare tax, and so is the employer on that wage.
asks.published_now: Nothing. The exemption has no published cost.
asks.request: An annual estimate of wages paid under the student FICA exemption and the resulting Social Security and Medicare tax forgone, nationally and by state.
asks.would_settle: What the exemption costs. It is a subsidy of roughly 15.3% of payroll that applies only when the worker is foreign, and it is the clearest cash incentive in the system to prefer one. Nobody has published its size.

evidence.label: forgone per $100,000 of payroll, employer and employee side together -- the statutory rate, not an estimate

asks.held_by: Internal Revenue Service, Tax Exempt and Government Entities
asks.title: Form 990 employee counts that are populated
asks.collected_on: Form 990 Part V, which carries the W-3 employee count.
asks.published_now: The field, frequently as zero even where the filing reports staff elsewhere.
asks.request: Either a populated field or a documented explanation of when it is left blank.
asks.would_settle: Sizing an organization by people rather than by money. Revenue is the only usable measure of a cap-exempt sponsor today, and revenue is not a count of anything.
